name: Steamed cassava
summary: Steamed cassava, told three ways. Người Lao Động says pandan or coconut cream, or the root ground for bánh tằm. Báo Quốc tế says pandan, sesame salt, and coconut cream together. Tuổi Trẻ names khoai mì hấp at two markets.
origin: Củ Chi. Người Lao Động, crediting Ngôi sao, on 6 Mar 2017, and Báo Quốc tế on 11 Aug 2024, both tie steamed cassava to the tunnels and to the wartime years. Tuổi Trẻ, on 5 May 2024, names it at chợ Củ Chi and chợ Việt Kiều.
howToEat: Người Lao Động gives two steamings, and does not fold them into one plate: steamed with pandan, or steamed with coconut cream. The same account also grinds the root for bánh tằm.
Báo Quốc tế describes one plate: steamed, with pandan and sesame salt, mixed with coconut cream already cooked. That account stays beside the two steamings.
No price was printed. Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Người Lao Động says it is sold along the roads toward Củ Chi and cooked for people who visit the tunnels.
Báo Quốc tế says it is common around the tunnels.
Tuổi Trẻ names khoai mì hấp at chợ Củ Chi and chợ Việt Kiều and prints no street number.
seoDescription: Steamed cassava in Củ Chi. Pandan or coconut cream on one account, both together on another. The price is Check on arrival.
taste: Người Lao Động calls Củ Chi cassava fragrant and sweet, crisp-chewy or rich. Báo Quốc tế calls the steamed root chewy and fragrant, rich from coconut cream, with a light sweetness.
